result.title: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention
result.summary: Autonomous research agents are increasingly used to automate large portions of scientific research, yet they are prone to research integrity violations (RIVs): behaviors that compromise the validity, reproducibility, or faithfulness of the research process. We present RIDAR, a framework for automated RIV detection and runtime intervention. First, we introduce RIVT, a comprehensive taxonomy of 14 RIV types spanning the full research lifecycle. Building on RIVT, we present RIDAR-post-hoc, a framework to detect RIVs within agent trajectories. RIDAR-post-hoc achieves 85.2% F1 performance on RIV-Gold, a benchmark for RIV detection with 60 expert-annotated trajectories. Applying RIDAR-post-hoc to RIV-Wild, a dataset of 300 agent trajectories across 50 distinct research tasks, we detect 3,964 RIV instances in 99.7% of trajectories, revealing the prevalence of RIVs in current agents. Finally, we present RIDAR-runtime, a framework for dynamically detecting and correcting RIVs during agent runtime. RIDAR-runtime effectively reduces agent RIVs remaining at task completion by 36.8%. We will release our code and data to facilitate future research.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 RIDAR 框架：先构建覆盖研究全流程的 14 类研究诚信违规（RIV）分类法，再给出对 agent 轨迹的事后检测方法（RIV-Gold 上 F1 为 85.2%）与运行时检测纠正方法，报告任务结束时残留违规下降 36.8%。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「过程忠实性」违规的轨迹级自动检测与运行时干预思路，可能为审计 latent 推理轨迹是否真正依据视觉证据、以及在生成中纠偏提供类比线索，但检测信号能否迁移到多模态推理尚待核查。
